note:
# Census pass: P-E-2018-93840-dffa6997

## What the paper is
One dimensionless ODE. Market growth with a carrying capacity minus an environmental
damage term gives dM/dtau, the fixed points of that derivative are read as a country's
equilibria, and the parameter plane (s, r) is carved into stable, vulnerable and fragile
regions by the saddle-node bifurcation where two fixed points coalesce. Three countries
are then planted in that plane: Syria, Cuba and New Zealand. Twenty-four physical pages,
seven printed exhibits, all figures, no tables.

## Coverage arithmetic
Thirteen measured regions on eleven of the twenty-four pages, and they close exactly:
seven figure rows plus six exclusions, no unaccounted region and no missing exhibit - the
first census in this stretch with no deficit and no tables at all.

The six exclusions are all apparatus of one kind or another: four are equation images (the
dimensional model on p4, the fixed-point condition on p7, the root equation on p8 and the
tangency derivative on p11), one is the official MCM control-number block on the summary
sheet, and one is a thin full-width band on p8 that turns out to be the running head and
its rule - rasterised, so the region pass boxes it like a picture.

## Caption side and the caption that is not text
All seven captions print BELOW their art, so this paper is a constant on the field that
split #169 down the middle. It is not a constant on caption content: these captions are
declarative sentences rather than noun phrases, and they show the copy-paste seam plainly
- 'Figure 2: This gure depicts the relationship between dMdt = dMdt and M', where the
symbol was pasted onto itself. Three of the seven carry an interpretation the body then has
to accept ('The model predicts that Syria would have a negative growth rate and become
more fragile').

Figure 1's caption is the paper's trap in the other direction from #169's. #169's notation
table had a printed caption line that the text layer never contained; here the caption is
two full sentences of prose, sitting under the paper's central chart, and the text layer
contains no trace of either sentence. It is recorded typed-from-crop.

## What the figures are made of
Seven exhibits, one family: line. Four of them draw solution curves in the (M, dM/dt) plane
- which is simply the plane the ODE lives in, so the chart choice is forced by the model
rather than chosen by the author. Figure 1 makes the same argument one dimension down, in
x, to show the fold by hand; the last two are the analytical charts: Figure 3 maps the
(s, r) parameter plane into the three state regions, and Figure 6 reuses those same
boundary curves to plant the three countries inside them.

Exactly one figure prints tick numbers (Figure 3). The other six print tick marks with no
numerals at all, which means the paper's claims about growth rates, upward shifts and
approach to equilibrium cannot be checked against any exhibit it prints. Three charts
carry legends inside the frame, four carry no legend and label the curves in place, and
not one is multipanel or three-dimensional.

Two title defects are worth recording because they are sentence-level, not layout-level:
Figure 3 is titled 'Plot of s vs t' while its axes are s and r, and Figure 6 is titled
'Country Analysis', the name of the section it sits in.

## Citation practice
This is the weakest citation pass in the lane so far. Only two of the seven figures are
ever numbered in the prose: Figure 1 ('In Figure 1, we see that for a fixed k...') and
Figure 2 ('...in Figure 2'). Figures 3 to 7 are pointed at by deixis alone - 'the resulting
graph is as shown below', 'As can be seen from the graph below', 'this bifurcation plot
positioned three countries' - and three of them (Figures 4, 5 and 7) are never referred to
by anything but their own caption. A reader who skips a page cannot know which exhibit the
prose means, and no count of exhibits catches that: the census records five rows with no
first_page, which is the only signal the schema has for a figure nobody points at.

## The layer's own defects
The text layer drops ligatures throughout: 'gure' for figure, 'di erent' for different,
'De ning' for Defining, ' re' for fire, 'su er' for suffer. Every deictic pointer sentence
above therefore has to be transcribed with its gaps intact, and any pipeline that repairs
the spacing will fail its own substring check. The running head reads 'Team # 93840 Page N
of 19' across 24 physical pages, so the folio is five pages short of the document. And one
identical red Chinese resale banner is stamped across the top of every page and appears
nowhere in the text layer - the same banner as #168's, in a different position.
rules: Every figure caption prints BELOW its art - seven of seven - and this paper has no tables at all, so caption side is a paper-level constant here rather than the split seen in #169 [caption.position].

The caption form is `Figure <n>: <sentence>`, colon, and unlike the last three papers the caption is a full declarative sentence, not a noun phrase: 'Figure 3: This gure is a parametric plot of (s; r), where s and r are expressed as a function of t.' [caption.numbering].

Captions run nineteen to thirty-four words, two sentences for six of the seven and one for Figure 6, and three of them carry an interpretation the body has to accept: 'The model predicts that Syria would have a negative growth rate and become more fragile.' [caption.concludes].

The first three captions name the variables they plot (r and k; M and dM/dt; s, r and t) and the last four name none - so the labelling discipline decays along the paper and the case-study captions are the bare ones [caption.variable_count].

One caption is not in the text layer at all: Figure 1's two sentences exist only as ink on p8, which is why the paper's most important exhibit is recorded caption_source=typed-from-crop [caption.verbatim].

Only TWO of the seven figures are ever numbered in the prose. Figures 3 to 7 are pointed at by deixis alone - 'the resulting graph is as shown below', 'As can be seen from the graph below', 'this bifurcation plot' - so five of seven exhibits have no first_page and no lead_pages at all [mention.first_page].

The two numbers that do appear are both inside the model section: Figure 1 is named on its own page ('In Figure 1, we see that for a xed k...') and Figure 2 one page early ('...in Figure 2.'), so every pointer in this paper is a zero- or one-page lead [mention.lead_pages].
Pointer style is split between naming and showing: Figure 1 uses the figure-n-shows form, Figure 2 the as-shown-in form, and nothing else is named [mention.lead_pattern].

The reading sentence follows immediately and always states a count or a direction: 'when r equals r1, the equation returns three roots, which means the function has three xed points' [mention.trail_sentence].

All seven figures are the same family - line - and five of them are the same chart: a family of solution curves drawn to expose the fixed points, four in the (M, dM/dt) plane where the ODE lives and one, Figure 1, in x [geometry.family].

Two figures leave that plane and they are the paper's two analytical charts: Figure 3 in (s, r) parameter space with the three state regions drawn as areas, and Figure 6 reusing the same boundary curves to plant the three countries inside them [geometry.family].
Not one figure is multipanel, shares an axis, carries a colourbar or is three-dimensional; the paper has no composite exhibit of any kind [geometry.panel_count].

Legends are inside the axes three times (Figures 4, 5, 7) and absent four times; where a legend is missing the curve is labelled in place instead ('Stable Status', 'Vulnerable Status', 'Fragile Status', or the country names) [geometry.legend].

Exactly one figure prints tick numbers - Figure 3, the parametric plot with axes 0 to 20 and 0 to 0.8. The other six print TICK MARKS with no numerals, so every claim the text makes about growth rates and shifts is unreadable from the exhibit [geometry.printed_numbers].

All seven charts carry an in-plot title and none relies on the caption for its label ('Analysis of Fixed Points', 'Dimensionless Function', 'Plot of s vs t', 'Fragility Assessment of Syria', 'Fragility Assessment of Cuba', 'Country Analysis', 'Fragility Assessment of New Zealand and Its Current State') [geometry.data_labels].

Titles are not reliable: Figure 3 is titled 'Plot of s vs t' while its axes are s and r, and Figure 6 is titled 'Country Analysis', which is the name of its section rather than a description of what it shows [caption.verbatim].

Legends are hand-built and hand-typed: Figure 7's key misspells its own label ('Equillbrum'), and Figure 5 adds a 'Current Position' key that Figure 4, drawn from the same script, does not have [geometry.legend].

The case-study triple is a copy-paste triple: Figures 4, 5 and 7 are the same assessment for three countries, and the hand-built legend is four keys for Syria, five for Cuba and two for New Zealand with no change of intent across them [geometry.legend].

Families are decided by the model, not by the data: because everything the paper computes lives in the derivative plane, no bar, scatter, histogram, box plot, heatmap, map, radar or pie appears anywhere in seven figures [geometry.family].

Exhibits are concentrated in the analytical half: Figures 1, 2 and 3 all sit under 5 Equilibrium and Tipping Points, and Figures 4 to 7 are spread across 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 - no exhibit at all stands in the introduction, the model derivation or the intervention section [place.section_kind].

The case studies get one figure each and no table anywhere, except Cuba, which gets two: its own assessment (Figure 5) and then the whole bifurcation diagram with the three countries planted in it (Figure 6), which is filed under 6.2 because that is where it happens to fall [place.section_path].

No exhibit owns a page, no page carries two of them, and the largest single exhibit covers 0.2807 of a page (Figure 1) while the smallest covers 0.1027 (Figure 4) - the difference between the model figures, which are drawn wide, and the case-study figures, which are drawn small in the corner of a page of prose [place.area_frac].

Document order equals number order throughout, so the paper has no numbering break - its citation failure is that five of the seven are never named, not that they are named out of order [place.doc_order].

Six of the thirteen measured regions are not exhibits: an equation image on p4, the fixed-point equation on p7, the roots equation on p8, the tangency derivative on p11, the official MCM control-number block on p1 and one thin full-width band on p8 that is the running head and its rule rasterised [place.section_path].
